inline_comments.comment:
`fs.watch` with `{ recursive: true }` is not supported on Linux before Node.js 22. On Linux with Node.js 18 or 20 (the minimum Storybook supports), the `recursive` flag is silently ignored—watchers will only cover the top-level directory, and changes to any source file in a subdirectory (i.e. nearly every component file in a real project) will never be detected. The existing `try/catch` only handles a thrown error; silent no-op is the real hazard. Before merging, either:
1. Add a platform/version check and fall back to manually watching each subdirectory with a `chokidar`-style recursive walk on Linux, or
2. Declare in docs that file-watching HMR requires Node.js 22+.

`this.commandLine.fileNames.includes(fileName)` is an O(n) linear scan. `ensureFiles` is called on every `extractPropsFromStories` invocation (which happens for every manifest refresh), so for a project with many dynamically added story files this becomes quadratic. Replace the array with a parallel `Set<string>` for O(1) membership tests, or check against `this.extraFiles` (the suggested set from the checkRootFilesUpdate fix) before pushing.

`watch: boolean` (required, not optional) in the `PresetPropertyFn` options type is inconsistent with how the preset is invoked. `writeManifests` calls `getManifests(presets)` without a `watch` argument, which passes `watch: undefined` through `presets.apply`. At runtime this is fine because `undefined` is falsy and `manager.startWatching()` won't be called, but the type is technically violated, and any future code performing `options.watch.toString()` would throw. Change to `watch?: boolean`.

`execSync('cp -rL ...')` and `execSync('mkdir -p ...')` are Unix-only shell commands. They will fail outright on Windows, making the entire test suite non-portable. Prefer Node.js built-ins: `fs.mkdirSync(dest, { recursive: true })` and a recursive copy using `fs.cpSync(src, dest, { recursive: true })` (available since Node.js 16.7), or at minimum import `ncp`/`fs-extra` which are already available in the monorepo.

Empty `catch {}` in `cleanup` silently swallows all errors. Per project conventions, even best-effort cleanup should log at debug level so failures are visible during local debugging and CI triage. At minimum: `catch (err) { /* best-effort */ console.error('[test-helpers] cleanup failed:', err); }`

The `--max_old_space_size` ceiling for `storybook:ui:build` was silently bumped from 4096 MB to 5120 MB. This is a 25% increase with no accompanying comment explaining why (e.g., the persistent TS LanguageService memory overhead). Add a comment in the commit or next to this line, or verify that this change is intentional and not a side-effect left over from local profiling.

general_comments.comment: `ComponentMetaProject.fsFileSnapshots` (shared across all projects via `ComponentMetaManager`) is a `Map` that grows indefinitely—there is no eviction policy. For long-running dev servers on large monorepos (e.g., Mantine with 9 tsconfig projects), every file touched by any project accumulates an entry with its mtime and snapshot. Over hours of editing this can become a significant memory sink. Consider evicting entries for files no longer tracked by any project (e.g., on `deleted` events), or capping the map size with an LRU policy.

The PR description mentions that `react-component-meta` adds `@volar/language-core` and `@volar/typescript` as runtime `dependencies` in `code/renderers/react/package.json`. Per project rules, before adding a new npm package import inside a monorepo workspace you must verify the package is declared in the specific workspace `package.json` of the importing file. The imports are in `code/renderers/react/src/...` and both packages are present in `code/renderers/react/package.json`, so this is correct. However, the `@types/node` and `typescript` peer packages that the new Volar APIs depend on at type-check time are not mentioned—confirm the type declarations resolve correctly in the renderer package's type context.

Several `catch` blocks across the new code (in `batchExtract`, `extractPropsFromStories`, `getOrCreateConfiguredProject`) log or silently swallow errors using template-interpolation of the error object, e.g., `` logger.debug(`Batch extraction failed: ${err}`) ``. String-interpolating an `Error` object produces `[object Error]` rather than the message. Use `err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)` or log `err` directly as a second argument to `logger.debug` so the stack trace is preserved.

The test file `componentMetaExtractor.checker.test.ts` (2311 lines) is described as "copies of the tests in `componentMetaExtractor.test.ts`". Having two near-identical test suites with 2000+ lines each doubles the maintenance burden—any change to extraction behavior requires updating both files. Consider factoring the shared test fixtures and assertions into a parameterised helper so both the one-shot `createVirtualProgram` path and the persistent LS path run against the same suite with a single point of truth.
